title: Contextual telemetry scrubbing and retention tiers for observability pipelines
creator: Priya Desai
description: Build a privacy-first safety layer for observability ingestion and storage (the 'Privacy Fence + Chronicle') that applies contextual PII scrubbing, multi-tier retention, and access provenance. This ticket covers changes to tracing hooks, metrics/log pipelines, and dashboard storage policies so that tenant-sensitive fields are either pseudonymized or removed early in the pipeline, access to raw/derivative telemetry is logged and RBAC-controlled, and retention tiers are enforceable and queryable across hosted and Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing ingestion includes a configurable hook that executes tenant-aware scrubbing rules and returns a scrubbed payload or a pseudonymization token
Metrics/log pipelines enforce retention tiers: ephemeral (7d), short-term (90d), long-term (2y encrypted) with automated rollover
RBAC gates exist for access to raw telemetry; all access events are written to an immutable audit stream
Dashboards for latency/error expose scrub-failure rate, retention occupancy, and access-provenance metrics
E2E test harness demonstrates no PII leakage in 1000 synthetic traces across sampling levels and upload paths
Performance impact under normal load is <5% p90 ingestion latency increase; rollouts can be disabled per-tenant for emergency debug
updates: 2025-01-12: Spike completed — prototyped a tracing hook as a small Go service that applies JSON schema driven scrubbing rules. Observed 2.1ms median extra latency on local bench.

2025-01-20: Chosen pseudonymization approach: HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant salt stored in KMS; salts rotated quarterly. Trade-off: irreversible tokens reduce debug fidelity but greatly reduce re-identification risk.

2025-01-28: Drafted retention enforcement design: ingestion tags records with retention_tier and route to appropriate storage class; scheduled compaction job moves data between tiers and applies encryption-at-rest for long-term tier.

2025-02-02: Security review kickoff — security team requested auditability for right-to-audit requests and JIT access model for SREs. Added action item to store access justification metadata for each audit entry.

2025-02-04: Implemented initial RBAC prototype using service-account-scoped policies in the control plane; created audit stream consumer that writes to immutable ledger (append-only) for 90-day retention of access events.
comments: Nora (PM): Ensure this integrates with Console's per-route dashboards so customers can see how retention is applied to their routes.
Eli (Design): We need a compact UX for 'request raw telemetry' flow that includes a disclosure and automated TTL. Design to provide mockups by 2025-02-10.
Security (review): Add plan for key rotation, emergency key-revocation, and proof-of-deletion for long-term tier when requested by customer compliance.

Marco (assignee): Follow-up task to author migration script for existing stored traces — applying scrub rules in-place could change indices; propose creating scrubbed copies and swapping aliases to avoid downtime.
SRE: Request ability to temporarily bypass scrubbing for on-call troubleshooting with JIT and recorded justification. Limit bypass to 1 hour and log both who and why.
decisions: Use HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant salt (KMS-protected) for pseudonymization tokens to avoid storing raw identifiers in the long-term tier.
Apply contextual scrubbing at ingestion edge (tracing hooks) rather than retroactive scrubbing to reduce leakage windows and limit downstream reprocessing cost.
Retention tiers will be enforced via routing tags; compaction jobs will be idempotent and operate on copies when possible to preserve availability during migration.
RBAC will be enforced in the control plane with audit stream writes to an append-only ledger for 90 days; long-term audit exports will require manual export requests and legal approvals.
